## Findings
- claim-1: The authors report computational verification only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-6@L46-L54|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: The stronger proposed statement is \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), and the source says a proof eluded the authors. [source-6@L56-L72|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-3: If an exact integral presentation is \(Q\cong\operatorname{coker}(B:\mathbb Z^u\to\mathbb Z^g)\), with Smith form \(\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_s,0,\ldots,0)\), \(d_i>1\), then \[ Q\cong\mathbb Z^{g-s}\oplus\bigoplus_{i=1}^s\mathbb Z/d_i,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=g-s+\max_p\#\{i:p\mid d_i\}. \]
- claim-4: No exact integral presentation matrix for \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\), nor a proof of its exactness, is supplied here; therefore no Smith-normal-form computation is presently justified.
## Strategy
- First specify admissible \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), the finite window beyond \(r\le4,\ n-r\le5\), and its nondegenerate cases.
- Derive an integral presentation \(Q\cong\operatorname{coker}(B)\) from Schur multiplication, and prove that its relation lattice is exact.
- Only then run sandboxed SNF on each finite case. If the Smith entries are \(e_1,\dots,e_\rho\ne0\), including units, record
  \[
  \operatorname{rank}Q=g-\rho,\qquad
  \operatorname{Tor}(Q)=\bigoplus_{e_i>1}\mathbb Z/e_i,
  \]
  \[
  \mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=g-\rho+\max_p\#\{i:p\mid e_i\}.
  \]
- Label every resulting row finite computational evidence only.

## Gaps
- No admissibility conditions, finite case list, presentation matrix, or exactness proof is supplied.
- Therefore no SNF computation is presently justified or executed.
- The conjectural assertions \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=\binom{a+b}{a}\) and \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\) remain unresolved.

## Next
- Supply and independently review an exact integral presentation for each selected nondegenerate case.
- Execute the prescribed sandboxed SNF computations afterward and report rank, nontrivial torsion factors, and \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)\).
